clauses.reason: The paragraph provides that the designation of Unalaska, Alaska, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 31 (Alaska) "be, and it is hereby," revoked, and the next sentence states the order "shall become effective at" "the close of business January 15, 1941." This is a one-time act with a stated effective moment, so the command was performed and exhausted at the close of business on January 15, 1941; the date is recorded as that day, and the order's own effective-date sentence is the end source. The loss of port status survives as an accrued consequence, not a continuing command. No later instrument in the held record revokes, amends or restores it by this order's number.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 8639 of January 14, 1941 (6 FR 455, Federal Register issue of January 17, 1941) revokes the designation of Unalaska, Alaska, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 31 (Alaska) and states "This order shall become effective at" "the close of business January 15, 1941." The revocation is a one-time act with a stated effective moment; it was performed and the command exhausted at the close of business on January 15, 1941. The loss of port-of-entry status is a surviving consequence of that executed act, not a continuing command. No instrument held in the repository revokes, amends or restores the designation by executive order. The working text is the official Federal Register page text (machine-extracted from the PDF, OCR), not an authenticated transcription.
